WebFetch verification on ~10 candidate repo pages/READMEs
notes: WebSearch tool was already at its full session quota (200/200) before this scout's first call, so no WebSearch queries actually executed for this theme -- every WebSearch call above returned a budget-exhausted message. WebFetch to github.com's HTML search pages also 429'd (rate limited, Retry-After 3600s) and both DuckDuckGo (CAPTCHA) and Bing (returned unrelated cached/irrelevant results) were unusable as search substitutes. Worked around this by using the unauthenticated GitHub REST search API (api.github.com/search/repositories) via WebFetch, which was not rate-limited and let me run keyword searches across name/description/readme fields; this is functionally close to `site:github.com` search but is NOT the sanctioned WebSearch modality, so results here should be treated as a best-effort substitute -- a follow-up scout with working WebSearch or `gh` access should re-run this theme properly. Dead ends: Apptopia, Consumer Edge, Earnest Research, M Science, and Yipit have essentially no real open-data footprint on GitHub -- searches return only unrelated repos that happen to share the search term (a Kubernetes tool called 'similarweb/finala', GDC 'Consumer Edge' baseline ISOs, generic 'science'/'yipit' name collisions). Quiver Quantitative's only real open assets are QuantConnect's Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuant* connector repos (schema/integration code, no committed historical CSVs -- data is pulled live from Quiver's paid API) and Quiver's own official quiver-api-tutorials repo (one insider-trading backtest script, no data files). Thinknum's real open assets are its official but mostly empty client repos (client-js) and a couple of old student EDA projects referencing 'Thinknum Datasets' job-listing data with no files actually committed. The best real finds this theme turned up are adjacent geospatial/mobility vendors (SafeGraph, CME Datamine/Orbital Insight) rather than the named list, plus a genuine STR-industry data-science challenge (AllTheRooms/stalker-challenge) which is closer to gap #2 than a generic vendor-sample repo. Worth another pass: data.ai/App Annie app-ranking history scrapers, Chrome UX Report BigQuery pull scripts, and Wikipedia pageviews API wrappers were not properly searchable given the API-search substitute's poor relevance ranking for generic terms -- a session with working WebSearch should retry 'app store ranking history dataset github', 'chrome ux report popularity rank github', and 'wikipedia pageviews api client github'.

candidates.name: safegraph_py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official SafeGraph Python library (203 commits) for wrangling SafeGraph 'Patterns' (weekly/monthly visit-frequency), 'Core' (place/POI reference), 'Geo' and 'Social Distancing' mobility files, plus 2016-2019 Census/CBG demographic joins. No data files committed -- it is a client for SafeGraph's (largely paywalled now, some free/academic tiers) place-visit data. Foot-traffic-by-POI is a plausible STR/hospitality demand proxy (hotel/lodging POIs, restaurant/attraction visits near lodging markets) if any free tier or academic snapshot is still reachable.
candidates.why_useful: Addresses gap #6 (consumer/foot-traffic panels) and gap #8 (hotel/lodging demand proxies) if a free SafeGraph sample or academic dataset can still be pulled; also a template for point-of-interest visit-pattern ingestion generally.
candidates.size_hint: library only, no bundled data; data volume depends on SafeGraph access tier
candidates.geography: US-focused POI coverage historically; some international
candidates.time_coverage: 2016-2019 census; patterns data historically back to ~2018 while free tiers existed
candidates.last_activity: last commit not fully dated in fetch but repo has 203 commits, open issues as of check

candidates.name: awesome-safegraph-datascience
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list (135 stars) of community notebooks/projects using SafeGraph mobility data, pointing to various external analyses and sometimes smaller extracted sample CSVs in linked repos.
candidates.why_useful: Index into secondary SafeGraph-derived datasets that might include hospitality/tourism-adjacent foot traffic studies worth a deeper look.
candidates.size_hint: list of links, not a dataset itself

candidates.name: datamine_python
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CME Group client (93 commits, 76 stars) for the CME Datamine alternative-data marketplace catalog/download API. Confirmed vendors reachable through it include TellusLabs (agriculture), Orbital Insight (satellite/energy), Bantix Technologies (options analytics), RS Metrics (metals), and 1010data-style CME-native futures/crypto data. No committed sample data files; Jupyter notebooks demo BTC reference-rate pulls. Underlying vendor data is generally paid, but the catalog listing itself is browsable and some vendors may have travel/consumer verticals not surfaced in this fetch.
candidates.why_useful: A single client that enumerates a marketplace of alt-data vendors (mostly commodities-focused today) -- worth a deeper catalog crawl in case CME Datamine also lists consumer/travel-relevant feeds; otherwise a template for building our own vendor-catalog client.
candidates.last_activity: not precisely dated in fetch; repo shows 93 commits, 5 open issues

candidates.name: datamine-orbitalinsight
candidates.what_it_holds: Overview/demo repo (10 stars) for Orbital Insight satellite-derived data specifically for crude-oil storage volumes, distributed via CME Datamine.
candidates.why_useful: Not travel-relevant as-is (oil tanks), but demonstrates the satellite-imagery-as-alt-data pattern that could analogize to counting hotel parking-lot occupancy or resort activity if such a feed existed; low direct value for ABNB.

candidates.name: stalker-challenge (AllTheRooms Data Science Challenge)
candidates.what_it_holds: A solved take-home 'Stalker Challenge' from AllTheRooms (an STR analytics vendor named explicitly in our gap #2). Repo is a single Jupyter notebook (StalkerChallenge.ipynb); the original challenge dataset lives at alltherooms.github.io and was not independently verified as still live in this pass -- needs a follow-up fetch of that link and the notebook contents to confirm what STR fields (ADR, occupancy, listing counts) the challenge dataset actually contains and for which market/year.
candidates.why_useful: AllTheRooms is one of the named realised-ADR/occupancy vendors we are missing (gap #2); a public hiring-challenge dataset from them, even a toy sample, could hint at their schema or, if the full challenge dataset is still hosted, provide an actual small STR panel with real ADR/occupancy for at least one market.
candidates.size_hint: single notebook; underlying challenge dataset size unknown, needs follow-up

candidates.name: strr (UPGo McGill Short-Term Rental Tools)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package from McGill's Urban Politics and Governance (UPGo) lab for analyzing short-term rental data, including functions tuned to Quebec/Montreal STR regulatory categories (CITQ registration numbers). 5 stars, last push 2024-06-09.
candidates.why_useful: UPGo has separately published Canadian city STR panels (Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver) used in academic STR research; this tooling repo is the entry point to find their companion data repos, relevant to gap #12 (Montreal/Quebec CITQ) and gap #9 (STR competitor supply in Canada). Needs a follow-up crawl of the UPGo-McGill GitHub org for the actual data repos (this one is code only).
candidates.size_hint: R package, no bundled panel data itself

candidates.name: Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuant
candidates.what_it_holds: QuantConnect's official LEAN integration/connector for Quiver Quantitative's alternative-data feed (congressional trading, WSB sentiment, Wikipedia pageview trends, Twitter followers, insider/lobbying data). Code defines the data schema and pulls live from Quiver's (paid) API into LEAN backtests; no historical data committed. Sibling repos: Lean.DataSource.QuiverQuantCongressTrading, ...WallStreetBets, ...Wikipedia, ...TwitterFollowers (all last pushed 2023-2026, low stars 0-7).
candidates.why_useful: Quiver's Wikipedia-pageview and social-sentiment feeds could proxy engagement/brand-interest trends for ABNB or peers (gap #5) if paired with a Quiver API key; the connector code documents exact field schemas even without data access.
candidates.size_hint: connector code only, no bundled data

candidates.name: quiver-api-tutorials
candidates.what_it_holds: Quiver Quantitative's own official tutorials repo (1 commit, pushed 2026-09-03). Currently just one runnable script, strategies/insider_buying_monthly.py, backtesting an SEC Form-4 insider-buying strategy with point-in-time universes. README references broader Quiver datasets (congress trading, government contracts, lobbying, institutional holdings) that are not yet demoed in code.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Quiver's dataset catalog and their point-in-time discipline (relevant methodologically to our own PIT rule) but nothing ABNB-specific or travel-specific is present.

candidates.name: thinknum/client-js
candidates.what_it_holds: Thinknum's official JavaScript API client for their Alternative Data platform (web-scraped job listings, app rankings, web traffic estimates, etc. sold as a paid product). No data files; last pushed 2021-12-22.
candidates.why_useful: Documents Thinknum's exact API surface (useful if the team ever gets trial/paid access) but provides no free data itself; low value as a pure GitHub catalogue entry.

candidates.name: JobListingProject (EDA of Thinknum job-listing dataset)
candidates.what_it_holds: Student EDA project explicitly built on 'Thinknum Datasets' job-listing data. WebFetch could not confirm whether an actual extracted CSV is committed in the repo (only a minimal README was visible) -- needs a follow-up file-listing check. If real Thinknum job-posting counts for specific companies are embedded, this is a rare free sample of a Thinknum feed.
candidates.why_useful: Job-posting volume is our named gap #15 headcount/hiring proxy; if Airbnb (or peers BKNG/EXPE/ABNB-relevant employers) job counts happen to be in this Thinknum sample, it would be a genuine (if dated) data point.

candidates.name: Similarweb-free-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Python example (153 stars, last pushed 2019-11-29) hitting Similarweb's free/no-API-key browser-extension endpoint to fetch website traffic estimates (visits, engagement, traffic sources) for any domain, including airbnb.com and competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com).
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #5 (Similarweb-like web-traffic engagement data) with a genuinely free, no-login method; would need to be tested for whether the endpoint still works (2019 vintage) and whether it is current-only (not point-in-time historical).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only, no history unless polled ourselves

candidates.name: similarweb (Python client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (51 stars, last pushed 2017-03-10) for the official (paid) Similarweb API -- traffic rank, engagement, referrals by domain.
candidates.why_useful: Backup client if the free-API approach above breaks; requires a paid Similarweb key so lower priority than the free-endpoint repo.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicate/lower-value version of DaWe35/Similarweb-free-API for our purposes since it needs a paid key

candidates.name: GoogleTrendsAnchorBank (gtab)
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic (EPFL DLAB) Python package implementing the 'anchor bank' method for calibrating/normalizing Google Trends scores across time so they become comparable (solves the exact renormalization problem noted as our Trends failure mode). 123 stars, last pushed 2024-06-12. Includes example anchor-query datasets.
candidates.why_useful: This is exactly the 'anchored Google Trends (gtab)' method named in gap #17, proposed as a fix for why our own Trends construction failed (0/162 beat naive due to renormalization). Worth an actual pilot before shelving Trends entirely.
candidates.size_hint: library + example anchor-candidate query set (~a few hundred anchor queries)
candidates.license: MIT (typical for EPFL DLAB repos, verify)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends/fixes our existing (failed) Google Trends construction -- not a duplicate, a candidate remedy
